nccl-tests bandwidth figures. algbw = bytes/time; busbw applies an algorithm factor (all-reduce 2(n-1)/n) so it compares with link bandwidth.
PCIe Advanced Error Reporting: kernel counters and messages for correctable and uncorrectable PCIe errors.
Collective that sums (or otherwise reduces) a buffer across all ranks and gives every rank the result. Used for gradients in data-parallel training.
Baseboard Management Controller: an independent controller on the server board for sensors, logs, console and power control.
Hours of stress on new hardware while logging temperature, power, clocks and errors, to catch early failures before customers do.
Container Device Interface: a declarative spec describing device nodes and mounts for a container runtime.
A limit that stops automated remediation when too many nodes look unhealthy at once.
nvidia-smi fields explaining why GPU clocks are lowered (power cap, thermal, hardware slowdown). Formerly called throttle reasons.
A communication operation involving a group of ranks: all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter, all-to-all, broadcast.
NVIDIA Data Center GPU Manager: health, diagnostics (levels r1-r4), policy and telemetry for data-center GPUs.
Exports DCGM fields as Prometheus metrics.
Data Center Quantized Congestion Notification: congestion control for RoCE using ECN marks.
Kubernetes mechanism that advertises devices such as nvidia.com/gpu as countable node resources.
Dynamic Resource Allocation: Kubernetes API (GA in v1.34) for claiming devices by attributes via ResourceClaims and DeviceClasses.
Error-correcting code memory. Single-bit errors are corrected; double-bit (uncorrectable) errors kill the affected work.
Elastic Fabric Adapter: AWS network interface for HPC/AI with an OS-bypass transport (SRD) used through libfabric.
NVIDIA tools to run containers unprivileged on HPC systems; Pyxis adds srun --container-image to Slurm.
Starting all pods or processes of a distributed job together, or none of them.
NIC reads and writes GPU memory directly, bypassing host memory.
Slurm generic resources, such as GPUs, declared in gres.conf and requested with --gres.
NVIDIA's multi-GPU server baseboard design (e.g. 8 GPUs connected by NVSwitch).
Lossless, credit-based high-performance fabric managed by a subnet manager; common in large training clusters.
Older binary protocol for out-of-band server management; largely superseded by Redfish.
Stored attention keys and values for generated tokens; its size per token sets how many sequences fit on a GPU.
Model FLOPs Utilization: achieved model FLOPs divided by the hardware's peak FLOPs.
Multi-Instance GPU: hardware partitioning of A100/H100-class GPUs into isolated instances.
Multi-Process Service: lets several processes share a GPU concurrently with limited isolation.
NVIDIA Collective Communications Library: GPU-to-GPU collectives over NVLink, PCIe and networks.
Node Health Check: HPC framework run as a Slurm health check or prolog to drain bad nodes.
Non-Uniform Memory Access: memory and devices attached to one CPU socket are faster for that socket.

Priority Flow Control (pause frames for lossless classes) and Explicit Congestion Notification (marking packets), used together in RoCE networks.
Fabric layout where NIC k of every node connects to the same set of leaf switches.
Remote Direct Memory Access: a NIC reads or writes remote memory without the remote CPU or kernel copies.
DMTF standard REST/JSON API for server management exposed by BMCs.
RDMA over Converged Ethernet, version 2: RDMA carried in UDP (port 4791) over IP networks.
Replacing bad GPU memory rows with spares; pending remaps apply after a GPU reset (XID 63 event, XID 64 failure).
System Event Log kept by the BMC: power, thermal and hardware events.
A rank slower than the others; collectives wait for it, so it slows the whole job.
Time to first token and inter-token latency: the two main latency metrics for LLM serving.
NVIDIA driver error code written to the kernel log as 'NVRM: Xid'.
Optimal checkpoint interval ~ sqrt(2 x checkpoint cost x mean time between failures).
